prompt_text: Who is the best interior painting company in St. Louis MO?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t objectively pick a single “best” company for you, because the right painter depends on your budget, the type/age of your home, the finishes you want, and your schedule. I can, however, help you find the best option for your needs. A good next step is one of two choices — either tell me your ZIP code and any preferences (budget, timeline, eco‑friendly paints, historic home, one room vs whole house) and I’ll give a short vetted shortlist and questions to ask, or use the checklist and scripts below to evaluate local bids yourself.

How to choose the best interior painter
- Check reviews and credentials: read recent Google, Yelp, Angi, and BBB reviews. Confirm company is insured and, if required, licensed for St. Louis/MO.
- Look at real work: ask for photos of similar jobs and 2–3 local references you can call.
- Verify prep and materials: a professional will describe prep (patching, sanding, priming, masking), which paint brands they use, and recommended sheen.
- Confirm crew size & timeline: who will be onsite, how long, work hours, and cleanup expectations.
- Get a written contract: scope, colors/brands, number of coats, start/finish dates, payment schedule, and warranty/guarantee.
- Compare 3 bids: don’t take the cheapest without verifying scope; very low bids often skip prep.
- Ask about extras: dust containment, odor/low‑VOC options, furniture moving, trim/cabinet refinishing.

Key questions to ask when getting estimates
- Are you licensed and insured? Can you provide a certificate of insurance?
- How many coats do you include? Do you prime where needed?
- What paint brands and VOC levels do you use?
- Do you provide a written estimate and contract?
- Can you show before/after photos and local references?
- What is your warranty on labor and touchups?
- How do you handle unexpected repairs or extra work?

Red flags
- No written contract
- Requests large upfront payment (more than a normal deposit ~10–30%)
- Unwillingness to provide references or photos
- Poor communication or inconsistent arrival times during estimate

Typical cost ranges (ballpark)
- Per room: often $300–$1,000+ depending on size and prep
- Per square foot: roughly $2–6 per finished sq ft in many markets
(Exact cost varies widely with prep, ceilings, height, trim, and finishes.)

If you want, I can:
- Provide a short list of well‑reviewed painters near your ZIP code (tell me the ZIP).
- Draft an email/phone script and a side‑by‑side estimate comparison sheet.
- Help evaluate 2–3 written estimates if you paste them here.

Which would you prefer?
